title: Version-Controlled Search: The Web as It Was — Ryan Ahern, Exa
talk_summary: Exa's Ryan Ahern pitches agentic web search and a new 'Snapshot' feature that stores 400B+ versioned web pages so you can run a search as it would have returned at a past date. The practical core is backtesting: replaying agentic search features against historical web state to check whether a signal is predictive or overfit, instead of waiting months on live data.

takeaways.technique: Backtest agent features against point-in-time snapshots
takeaways.what_they_do: They store versioned copies of crawled URLs and let you re-run a search 'as of' a prior date, so an agentic feature can be evaluated on data that existed before the outcome was known, avoiding label leakage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can go back and like set up your your your e-vals and your identic harness in such a way that you can detect these things
takeaways.numbers: 400 billion plus snapshots of the web

takeaways.technique: Holdout set to detect overfitting to eval features
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that agents trained on a live set can overfit (their example: a feature literally 'is the company named Dominion'), so they split sample sets and check generalization against a holdout.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also try and check that it generalizes

takeaways.technique: Snippet-level retrieval instead of full pages
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of returning full pages or one page's highlights, they extract the exact snippets across all results needed to complete the trajectory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can actually get higher quality results at 95% fewer tokens than you would at full page text
takeaways.numbers: 95% fewer tokens vs full page text

takeaways.technique: Optimize total trajectory cost, not per-tool-call cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the metric that matters is the cost of the whole agent task, and that fewer, higher-quality retrieval calls reduce downstream inference cost and failure rate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the fewer tool calls that it needs to make, the more cost-effective on your inference
